units.translation: ⟦1⟧, however, is not deictic, referring to an actual voting pebble held in the hand, but is to be understood with reference to the preceding verse. In Euripides (⟦2⟧, I.T. 965, 1472) the representation is no different; he traces the principle of acquittal on a tie vote back to this case. Athena ostensibly motivates her vote for Orestes mythologically: being herself a woman, she would, as someone might think, have to be for the woman; but as the motherless daughter of Zeus she votes for the man. In fact, however, the true nature of the matter emerges in v. 739f.: the murderess of her husband deserves no vengeance; for ⟦3⟧ . . ⟦4⟧ means 'her husband'.
── 736 ⟦1⟧ (not ⟦2⟧) is regular; see Kühner-Gerth, Synt. II, 403, n. 7. On 738 Abresch compares ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧.
others again love mothers more than father

── 741 Orestes is the victor, even if the verdict is by equal votes? Rather, the present ⟦1⟧ is used of what is indeed future but is immediately given along with another future event, as in ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, Kühner-Gerth I, 136. Below at 744 stands ⟦5⟧, not ⟦6⟧.
742 f. presuppose the custom, which also existed later, that the votes were counted out by some judges specially appointed for the purpose, Aristot. ⟦1⟧. ⟦2⟧. Col. 35, 28 ⟦3⟧.
those who have been allotted to the votes count them out
The ⟦1⟧, however, are called here and at 753 ⟦2⟧ 'lots', from the similarity of the procedure in casting lots and in voting.

⟦1⟧ exactly like ⟦2⟧ of commission and office, ⟦3⟧. 744-753 counting and announcement of the result. During the counting so much is said that one imagines a larger number than 12 voting, especially also according to Apollo's words at 748 ff.

── 746 ⟦1⟧ like ⟦2⟧ (⟦3⟧); ⟦4⟧ the last resort of despair, probably more proverbial than literal, after passages such as ⟦5⟧ (Pentheus speaks) ⟦6⟧; ⟦7⟧ (Demophon) ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, Aristoph. Ach. 125 etc. (Wecklein). ── 747
are these things not worthy of a terrible hanging?
and these things are near to hanging

⟦1⟧: we too are risking something, not you alone. ⟦2⟧ 301, 884; ⟦3⟧ in the active is no less correct than at v. 1017 ⟦4⟧; ⟦5⟧ 'henceforth, further' (often spatial, as ⟦6⟧). ── ⟦7⟧ concrete, plural because from two urns whose contents had to be kept apart. The scholiast wrongly speaks of black and white stones.
dwelling in the city of Pallas
